facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) remove different classes of uncertainty.
facts.quote: The three loops remove different classes of uncertainty.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) is the most economical stage for very large test volumes.
facts.quote: **SIL** is where very large test volume is most economical.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) exercises software requirements, decision thresholds, timing logic, state transitions, threat metrics, degradations and regression across thousands or millions of scenarios.
facts.quote: It exercises software requirements, decision thresholds, timing logic, state transitions, threat metrics, degradations and regression across thousands or millions of scenarios.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot show whether the production processor misses deadlines.
facts.quote: It cannot show whether the production processor misses deadlines

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot show whether the CAN or J1939 interface has unexpected timing behaviour.
facts.quote: whether the CAN or J1939 interface has unexpected timing behaviour

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot show whether the hydraulic and mechanical brake chain behaves as modelled.
facts.quote: whether the hydraulic and mechanical brake chain behaves as modelled.

facts.text: Extensions of the V-model for systems incorporating machine learning treat software-in-the-loop (SIL) as the first closed-loop stage.
facts.quote: Extensions of the V-model for systems that incorporate machine learning treat SIL as the first closed-loop stage.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) connects a real ECU and its real interfaces to a deterministic real-time plant simulation driving physical or emulated I/O, exercising communications, timing and faults before full-machine testing.
facts.quote: a real ECU is connected to a deterministic real-time plant simulation that drives physical or emulated I/O, so communications, timing and faults are exercised before full-machine testing.

facts.text: Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) is established across automotive, aerospace and industrial controls, including an older independent heavy-truck controller precedent.
facts.quote: It is established across automotive, aerospace and industrial controls, with older independent heavy-truck controller precedent

facts.text: No off-road perception-AEB end-to-end hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) case was found.
facts.quote: no off-road perception-AEB end-to-end HIL case was found.

facts.text: Conventional hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) does not prove optical or RF perception unless real sensor front ends are physically stimulated.
facts.quote: Conventional HIL does not prove optical or RF perception unless real sensor front ends are physically stimulated

facts.text: Radar and lidar target simulators have limited fidelity.
facts.quote: radar or lidar target simulators have limited fidelity.

facts.text: The natural hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) interface for the heavy off-road collision mitigation programme is the ISO/TS 21815-2 J1939 intervention interface.
facts.quote: For this programme the natural HIL interface is the ISO/TS 21815-2 J1939 intervention interface.

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) adds the actual vehicle or machine to testing.
facts.quote: **VIL** adds the actual vehicle or machine.

facts.text: IDIADA injects virtual hazards into a real vehicle's ECU on a track for vehicle-in-the-loop testing.
facts.quote: IDIADA injects virtual hazards into a real vehicle's ECU on a track

facts.text: An augmented-reality proving-ground vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) platform was published in 2024.
facts.quote: an augmented-reality proving-ground VIL platform was published in 2024

facts.text: A 2024 survey of testbench vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) describes physical sensor stimulation and whole-vehicle testing as a bridge between simulation and road tests.
facts.quote: a 2024 survey of testbench VIL describes physical sensor stimulation and whole-vehicle testing as a bridge between simulation and road tests

facts.text: A 2024 survey of testbench vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) identifies different accuracies among stimulation and testbench approaches.
facts.quote: identifying different accuracies among stimulation and testbench approaches

facts.text: A 2024 survey of testbench vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) identifies substantial equipment cost.
facts.quote: and substantial equipment cost.

facts.text: dSPACE material shows an intended road-vehicle testing chain that stimulates camera, radar and ultrasound while observing the response through to brakes and steering.
facts.quote: dSPACE material shows the intended road-vehicle chain: stimulate camera, radar and ultrasound while observing the response all the way to brakes and steering.

facts.text: Nothing beyond research was found for off-road vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL).
facts.quote: For off-road VIL, nothing beyond research was found

facts.text: No public, independent case was found of complete vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) validation of camera, radar, lidar or ultrasonic automatic braking on mining, quarrying or construction equipment.
facts.quote: a public, independent case of complete VIL validation of camera, radar, lidar or ultrasonic automatic braking on mining, quarrying or construction equipment was **not found**.

facts.text: The recommended testing hierarchy uses software-in-the-loop (SIL) for test volume.
facts.quote: The sensible hierarchy is SIL for volume

facts.text: The recommended testing hierarchy uses hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) for timing, interfaces and faults.
facts.quote: HIL for timing, interfaces and faults

facts.text: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) is recommended only where its extra physical fidelity justifies the investment.
facts.quote: VIL only where its extra physical fidelity justifies the investment

facts.text: The recommended testing hierarchy uses the real machine for actual stopping, terrain and environment.
facts.quote: the real machine for actual stopping, terrain and environment.
